earlier_scan.source_named: Stilo, Donald L. 1981. 'The Tati language group in the sociolinguistic context of Northwestern Iran' (Iranian Studies 14), pp. 175-176 on Maraghei; no fuller phonology located

sources.citation: Borjian, Habib. 2021. The Languages of Taleqan and Alamut. In Essays on Three Iranian Language Groups: Taleqani, Biabanaki, Komisenian. (JSTOR doi:10.2307/j.ctv27957fn.7) -- publisher preview only.
sources.note: Preview (pp. 1-3) states Marāqei is a conservative Tati variety of 16 villages in Rudbār-e Alamut (citing Yarshater 1967; Stilo 2018b, 2019) and that 'Only the Pašāi type, designated here as Alamuti, is incorporated in this comparative study'; its sec. 2.4 'Stress' (p. 5, not in preview) therefore concerns Taleqani/Pašāi Alamuti, not Maraghei.

sources.citation: Markaz-e Dāʾerat al-Maʿāref-e Bozorg-e Eslāmi. 'Tāti'. Dāneshnāme-ye Bozorg-e Eslāmi vol. 14, art. 5644 (online at lib.eshia.ir).
sources.note: Has a stress paragraph (past-tense stem-final stress, nouns/adjectives final stress, imperative initial) but it is explicitly about Takestani and Kolur Tati, citing Taheri 1371 p. 32 -- not Maraghei. On Maraghei it only says speakers call their dialect Marāghi and consider it closer to Takestan/Buin-Zahra Tati (citing Parmoun p. 45). Saved as jina text; not a Maraghei statement.

sources.citation: Rasouli, Hoseyn-Ali. 1369/1990. Barrasi-ye guyesh-e Marāghi dar rustā-ye Mushqin [A study of the Maraghi dialect in the village of Mushqin]. MA thesis, University of Tehran (Ancient Iranian Languages; supervisor Yahya Modarresi), 90 pp. Abstract reproduced in M.A. Naseh (ed.) 1386, Chekide-ye pāyān-nāme-hā-ye howze-ye zabān va zabānshenāsi 1333-1385, pp. 604-605.
sources.note: Only the 2-page abstract is online (archive.org item TatiMaraghi). It reports a phonological analysis (23 consonants, 8 simple vowels incl. /ö/ /ü/, 5 diphthongs /āy ay oy ow ey/) but says nothing about stress; the thesis body (which may) is not accessible.

sources.citation: Stilo, Donald L. 1981. The Tati language group in the sociolinguistic context of Northwestern Iran and Transcaucasia. Iranian Studies 14(3/4): 137-187.
sources.note: Silent. pp. 175-176 n. 3 and n. 6 only place Maraghei Tati in 16 villages of Rudbar-e Alamut incl. Dikin and note it is unintelligible to Pashei Tati speakers; Dikini/Maraghei data appear only in pronoun/isomap tables. The sole 'stress' hit is 'The point I wish to stress'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Maraghei dialect' and (fa) 'گویش مراغی'; Grokipedia 'Maraghei dialect'.
sources.note: No stress content in Wikipedia; fa refs add Yarshater 1348/1969 'Zabānhā-ye irāni-ye Alamut' (Kāveh, Munich, no. 27) and Parhizkari 1378/1999 'Guyesh-e Marāghi'. Grokipedia's 'likely word-initial stress' line is AI inference with no source and was disregarded.
